Ahmedabad, India, Mar. 23.—Mahatma Gandhi's 18-year-old adopted daughter, Laxmi, who belongs to the caste of untouchables, was arrested today in Taluka, Jalalpur, on a charge of distributing unlawful propaganda.

1932-05-11.text: (By United Press). Norfolk, Va., May 11.——Negotiations by John Hughes Curtis for return of the kidnaped Lindbergh baby have been transferred from here to a point off Block Island, it was reported persistently here today. Block Island lies between Long Island and the New England coast line. Curtis, the report said, has been in that area for the past four days during his absence from Norfolk. He is believed to be attempting to convince the purported kidnapers that no efforts are being made to trap them, This move, it was explained, has been made necessary because naval ships operating near the area in which Curtis had been attempting to establish contact had frightened the kidnapers.

(By The Associated Press) Miami, May 10--Captain W. N. Lancaster, former British army aviator, has been indicted for first degree murder in the strange shooting of Haden Clarke, fiancé of his flying partner, Mrs. Jessie Keith-Miller, Australian aviatrix. The true bill against Lancaster was returned by the Dade county grand jury yesterday a week after his arrest on a murder warrant, and Judge H. F. P. Atkinson ordered the filer held without bail for trial at circuit court term opening today. Lancaster Owned Pistol Clarke, 26 year old author, was fatally shot with a pistol owned by Lancaster April 21. He and Mrs. Keith-Miller, whose life story he was writing for publication, and at whose home he lived, became engaged while Lancaster, formerly her fiancé and for five years her flying partner, was in St. Louis on business. They wrote Lancaster of their plans to marry, but he telegraphed them

LONDON, May 10,—(/) Whether Ambassador Andrew W. Mellon will wear silk knee breeches for ordinary evening trousers when he attends the first of the royal courts at Buckingham Palace tomorrow night caused considerable interest among members of the American colony today. At the embassy nobody seemed to know the answer. One official who ordinarily would be informed said the ambassador’s apparel was a secret to him. A group of American women will be presented to King George and Queen Mary at the royal court.

London, May 10. (AP)— Whether Ambassador Andrew W. Mellon will or will not wear knee breeches at the first royal court at Buckingham Palace tomorrow night when a number of American women will be presented to King George and Queen Mary was a question embassy officials could not answer this morning. One official who ordinarily would know said he did not and added that furthermore, he was not raising the question with his chief. Ambassador Dawes aroused considerable comment when he broke with the traditions of the Royal Palace and appeared in ordinary evening trousers, but his predecessor, the late George Harvey, cut a particularly dashing figure at court in sombre, rather tight fitting breeches with bows at the knees and patent leather pumps.

London, May 11.—(A. P.)—Twelve American women will stand for one brief moment before Britain's king and queen tonight and hear the softly spoken words of presentation to royalty. They will then curtsey in solemn “thank you” for the regal favor and depart, tired, and perhaps wondering a bit, to their hotels. The moment of glory will be the climax of weeks of excitement and preparation—hours spent at dressmakers, the trip from America, long lessons in court etiquette, and hours spent in a queue of limousines in the Mall awaiting their turn to enter the palace. Besides Mrs. David K. E. Bruce, daughter of Ambassador Mellon, tonight's presentees include Miss Mary Elizabeth Beebe of Wallingford, Pa.; Miss Helen Bryan, Richmond, Va.; Mrs. Eugene H. Dooman, wife of the first secretary at the American embassy; Mrs. David E. Finley, Washington, D. C.; Miss Hilda Foster, Boston; Miss Estelle Frelin

London, May 11 (Wfi)—The liner Berengaria was reported aground today off Black Jack Buoy, in Southampton water. The liner was reported to have gone aground at half-tide while swinging to enter Southampton water. Six tugs were sent to aid and hoped to refloat her at high tide between 3 and 3:30 p.m. The Berengaria was inbound to Southampton from New York, whence she sailed on May 4, and was to have docked this morning. Among those on board are Mr. and Mrs. George Arliss, Sidney B. Wood, Jr., Rear Admiral Livingston Hunt, Dr. and Mrs. Serge Kowssey-itsky, and the United States team of women golfers captained by Marion Hollins.

| SOUTHAMPTON, England, May 11 (P)—The liner Berengaria, putting into this port today, ran aground off Calshot, 200 yards from Blackjack buoy. Six tugs pulled her off and she proceeded to her berth undemarcated.

VERSAILLES, France, May 10 (/) -Albert Francois Lebrun was elected fourteenth president of France today by a vote of 633 out of 747 cast to succeed the assassinated president, Paul Doumer. Paul Faure, noted Socialist leader, received 114 votes and 49 were blank. In the interest of harmony, there was virtually no opposition to the veteran statesman whose service as president of the Senate had put him in line for the presidency of the nation. Lebrun’s first act was to start for Elysee Palace to pay his respects at the bier of his slain predecessor. Then he was to go to the tomb of the Unknown Soldier and later in the day to the Luxembourg Palace to receive the diplomatic corps and high officials of the nation when they made their calls of congratulation.

1932-03-28.text: DUBLIN (#) — President Eamon De Valera’s government found itself fortified today to go ahead with the plan to abolish the oath of allegiance to King George. In demonstrations throughout the country Easter day thousands of men and women, members of the Republican army and other technically illegal organizations sounded a call for an Irish republic, supported De Valera’s plan to abolish the oath and the land annuities, and added that this was only part of the way they would go along the road to independence. In England, where the Irish question promised to be taken up immediately, reports said the Free State government would be backed by the independent labor party in parliament. A dispatch from Blackpool, where the party held its annual conference, quoted George Buchanan, independent labor member of parliament, as saying he and his colleague, James Maxton, would support De Valera’s plan.

By The Associated Press. Howling, northeast winds swept over New England today; full gales lashed the Atlantic coast; snow blanketed most of the east; and New York was drenched with rain, A blizzard struck northern New Hampshire, deepened the wet, heavy snow to seven inches in the forenoon, and continued unabated this afternoon. Heavy flakes snapped power lines in Pennsylvania. Parts of eastern Ohio suffered the heaviest snow in recent years. New York state is covered from the Adirondacks to the Pennsylvania line. Albany had more than six inches before noon, and state police reported that travel was precarious on many highways. Trolley service throughout the stormy sections was hampered, and in many places local railroad service was behind schedule. Chilly winds and mist held sway over the national capital and marred somewhat the annual Easter egg-rolling on the White House lawn.

Dublin, March 28 (UP)—Eamon De Valera will resume negotiations with Great Britain intended to abolish the oath and land annuity payments, backed by an Easter Sunday demonstration that the Irish Republican Army supports him. The roll of muffled drums Easter morning followed by the army’s peaceful march through the streets of Dublin and other cities confounded critics of the Republican Free State who had predicted violence. The army commemorated the 1916 Easter rebellion in a peaceful manner, just as De Valera promised it would. The army appealed for support of De Valera and repudiation of the Anglo-Irish Treaty of 1921. It restricted parade was the first since the Free State was formed. Men and youths drilled by night in mountain hideouts marched proudly before thousands of spectators. Their strength and degree of military perfection was a surprise to many who watched them converge on his

Dublin, March 28 (UP) —President Eamon de Valera drafted his reply to Great Britain today on the issues at dispute with the Irish Free State. The reply was understood to reiterate his intention of abolishing the oath to the crown and of retaining the land annuities, regardless of consequences. It will be submitted to the cabinet.

SHANGHAI, March 28 (CP) — Chinese and Japanese negotiations for a truce at Shanghai continued deadlocked today over the question of Japanese troop withdrawals. The Chinese delegates held steadfastly to their decision to accept no compromise on this phase of the question, declaring this was the order of the Nanking government. "They must either withdraw entirely or not at all," a spokesman said. "We will accept no gradual withdrawal." A spokesman for the Japanese said the parleys would be continued, however. The negotiators ran into further difficulties today over the sniping problem. The Japanese, claiming that sniping by Chinese civilians continued to be a serious menace to the lives of Japanese nationals, demanded some assurance that it would be stopped. The Chinese said the sniping was not authorized and that they could not be responsible for such activities.

Berlin—(—Paul Schwartz, believed to be the last German held as a prisoner of war, is coming home from France's “Devils Island,” Cayenne, after 12 years imprisonment. He is one of the few ever to come back from the island. His release is the climax of several months negotiations between his homeland and France. Born in Corsica of German parents, Schwartz was taken to Alsace Lorraine when he was a baby and there acquired German citizenship. At the outbreak of the war he joined the German troops and fought through the campaigns of the western front. Meanwhile his father died and his mother, forced from her house in the war area, had moved to Kiel. Attempting to reach his mother after the war, Schwartz found Kiel occupied by French troops. In the absence of his traveling pass, he was arrested by the French and because of his Corsican birth was convicted of high treason in taking up arms agai

1932-05-03.text: Miami, Fla.—Capt. W. N. Lancaster, British flier, was in jail today charged with first degree murder in the shooting of Hayden Clarke, writer and fiancé of Mrs. Jessie Keith-Miller, woman aviator. Authorities said Lancaster has confessed to forging two suicide notes. The flier was detained yesterday on a warrant sworn to by State’s Attorney N. Vernon Hawthorne, who said he probably would go before the Dade County grand jury today to seek an indictment. Hawthorne has exonerated Mrs. Keith-Miller in whose home the two men were guests at the time of the shooting April 21. He said she would be called as a grand jury witness.

LONDON, May 3. (P)—Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald will undergo an operation on his eye immediately, an official announcement today from No. 10 Downing Street said. The prime minister's left eye was operated on several weeks ago. His vision was affected, but reports that he might have to retire from active life were denied by his physician.

Victoria, B. C. May 3-7—The dominion government came to the aid of British Columbia today in an attempt to make the Doukhobors keep their clothes on. Nettled by Sunday's riot at Thrums, when police sprayed nude paraders with pepper powder and arrested 118 men and women, officials of province and dominion said they would settle the Doukhobor problem once and for all. The members of the sect must wear clothes, send their children to school and observe all other laws or go to prison for long terms, authorities said. Notified that another nude parade was planned, provincial officials warned the federal department of justice it might be necessary to arrest as many as 500, and that the province’s prison could not hold them. In Ottawa, a plan to herd the Doukhobors into a compound was under consideration. Meanwhile, authorities solved the problem of where to hold the trials of 118 prisoners, ma

By The Associated Press. London, May 2.-Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald may have to undergo an operation on his right eye similar to the surgical treatment of his left eye exactly four months ago tomorrow. This was disclosed today after a two hour examination of Mr. MacDonald's eyes, and his physicians decided to hold a consultation tomorrow to decide on the best course of treatment. Another specialist may be called in.

SHANGHAI, May 3 (#)—A band of 100 Chinese students attacked and painfully injured Quo Tai-Chi, Chinese vice minister for foreign affairs, and principal delegate at the peace parleys, here today. As a result, resumption of the parleys was indefinitely postponed. The mob attacked Mr. Quo as he was leaving his home in the French concession. As the students pummeled the minister, they accused him of intending to sign an agreement unfavorable to China.

By United Press SHANGHAI, May 3.—United States Infantry troops forced a Japanese raiding party to retire from the American defense sector of Shanghai tonight after a Japanese raid in which the doughboys were called out to defend Chinese civilians from the raiders. The Japanese retired stubbornly, threatening to return in force regardless of the Americans if any more stones were thrown by Chinese across the creek into the Japanese sector.

1932-05-19.text: Aden, Arabia, May 17 (®)— Shipping agencies feared that more than 300 persons may have perished aboard the blazing French motorship Georges Phillipar off Cape Guardafui, Italian Somaliland, as 254 haggard, smoke-grimed survivors arrived here today. The British steamers Contractor and Mahsud brought the first refugees, who reported that up to 100 passengers were trapped in their burning cabins yesterday. Another 420 survivors were understood to be on the French liner Andrew Lebon, which took them off the Soviet tanker Sovietskaia Neft. Shipping said they believed at least 1,000 persons were aboard the lost vessel and that unless they were picked up by ships which have not yet reported by wireless or have reached the African coast in boats, they must have met a horrible death. Racked with anxiety for the safety of relatives and friends, the survivors told of harrowing scenes that ended the

(By The Associated Press). Geneva, May 18.—The burning alive of many men, women and children by the Liberian frontier military force was reported to the League of Nations today in a communication signed in behalf of “the American, British and French governments. These atrocities, the report asserted, were committed against tribesmen of the Kru coast. The Liberian delegate submitted a memorandum to the league’s Liberian commission confirming the burning of 44 villages and the killing of 81 men, 49 women and 29 children. The commission recommended to the league council that a representative be sent to the Kru coast to assist in pacifying the country and to bring about the return of 12,000 tribesmen who have fled their homes. Violence by the Liberian military force followed an inquiry by the league commission in the course of which many tribesmen accused the government of oppression. The Li

London, May 18. (AP)—Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald, who recently underwent an eye operation, left the nursing home today and returned to his official residence in Downing Street where he had lunch before going home to Lossiemouth, Scotland, to complete his convalescence. Dr. W. S. Duke-Leder examined Mr. MacDonald's right eye — the one operated on—and decided the prime minister could safely leave the nursing home.

LONDON, May 18. — (0) — Sylvia Pankhurst, noted British feminist, said today she was launching an appeal in England for a Lindbergh baby memorial fund which, she said, would be used "to do something for children" if Col. Lindbergh does not need the money. Miss Pankhurst's notion was born of reports that Col. Lindbergh had expended his entire fortune in the search for his kidnapped child. The move was typical of the sympathy felt for the Lindberghs here.

Chatham, Mass, May 19--The German flying boat DO-X reported at 7 a.m. E.S.T. to the Radfomarine Corporation station here that it was approximately 100 miles northeast of Cape Cod, heading for Cape Sable. The weather was clear. The DO-X was making between 80 and 100 miles per hour. The huge craft, with passenger capacity for more than 100 persons, took off for Harbor Grace, Newfoundland, at 4:05 a.m. E.S.T., the first leg on its return flight to Lake Constance, Switzerland. The takeoff was from Manhasset Bay where the huge liner flew last night in order to take advantage of the longer, safer water runway. It was refueled and provisioned here yesterday afternoon. From Harbor Grace the DO-X will fly to the Azores, the second scheduled stop, if all goes well. From there she will hop to Lake Constance.

BOMBAY. May 19 (UP).--Bombay was threatened by plague today as the debris of five days of murder and arson lay in the streets and the waterworks remained closed as a precautionary measure against further riots. Fighting between Hindus and Moslems which had caused over 100 deaths and more injuries than the city’s hospitals could care for, spread to the mill area. Police were kept busy there trying to disperse gatherings of excited millhands. There were numerous stabbings and beatings. Police were forced to fire into mobs. Four persons were killed and 70 were injured last night in street fights in the shopping district. Many mills were closed forcibly by mill workers.

Tokyo, May 19. (Thursday). (P) A compromise cabinet with President Kisaburo of the dominant Seiyukai as premier was freely predicted today as an end to the national crisis brought about by the assassination of Premier Suyoshi Inukai. All of the political commentators in Tokyo morning newspapers were unanimous in their assertion that the next cabinet would be drawn in the main from the Seiyukai party but would include a few strong men from other factions. It was indicated Inukai, who succeeded the slain Inukai would probably receive the emperor's mandate to form a cabinet tomorrow.

HALIFAX, Nova Scotia—(AP)—The giant German airliner, DO-X arrived over here at ten Thursday morning on a flight from New York to Harbor Grace, New Foundland. It is on a return flight to Switzerland. The take off from New York was at 4 Thursday morning. A crew of fourteen is being carried by the huge craft.

1932-05-05.text: World Copyright, 1932, by United Press) LONDON—The British government was credited in well-informed circles today with the intention to propose at least a 25 per cent all-round reduction of war debts and reparations at the Lausanne conference meeting in June.

New London, Conn., May 5.—(AP)—The 60-foot speed boat Scipio of Bridgeport, an alleged rum runner, was captured off Fisher's Island after one of her crew had been wounded severely by a machine gun bullet from a coast guard boat. The wounded man, known to his shipmates only as Charlie, was shot in the head, the bullet fracturing his skull. Hospital officials said he would probably die. Coast guardsmen, who brought the Scipio to New London early today, said she carried 400 cases of liquor. Officials said the service vessel resorted to machine gun fire after the Scipio had ignored several warning shots from a one pounder.

MIAMI, FLA., May 4—(W.P.)—Captain W. N. Lancaster, former British flyer who is accused of killing Haden Clarke, fiancé of Mrs. Jessie Keith-Miller, today said he expected to have the entire case ‘settled’ within three weeks. “I won't seek bond as it is too expensive,” he told the United Press shortly after a Dade County grand jury had heard the evidence against him. “I have explanations for everything at the proper time,” Lancaster continued. “I hope I will be out and free within three weeks.” Clarke was found shot to death in the house shared by Mrs. Keith-Miller and Lancaster April 21. There were two notes nearby which indicated suicide but Lancaster has admitted he wrote them to cast suspicion from Mrs. Keith-Miller and himself. Mrs. Keith-Miller visited in jail late yesterday, bringing fresh linens to him.

Miami, Fla, May 5.—(?)—Mrs. Jessie M. Keith-Miller, Australian aviatrix, has joined in planning a defense for Capt. W. N. Lancaster, her British flying partner, in event he is indicted for murder of her young fiancé, Haden Clarke. “Everything brought out in the case has made Bill (Lancaster) look badly,” the woman flier said. “There are a thousand things to be brought out in fairness to him that are yet undisclosed.” Jurors Conclude Probe. The grand jurors concluded their inquiry into Clarke’s shooting yesterday, but probably will make no report before Saturday or Monday. Lancaster has been in jail three days on a murder charge. Clarke, who was collaborating with Mrs. Keith-Miller on a story of her life, was fatally wounded in her home where both he and Lancaster were guests a short time after the couple had disclosed to the captain their plans to marry. Both Lancaster and Mrs. Keith-Mil

New London, Conn., May 5 (UP)—Coast guard gunfire which perforated the rumboat Scipio of Bridgeport in more than 500 places today probably fatally wounded a mysterious rum runner known only to authorities as “Charley.” The Scipio, laden with 400 cases of liquor and carrying a crew of four, surrendered off Fisher’s Island after a machine gun bullet had pierced “Charley’s” skull. The man regained consciousness at the hospital here and a nurse asked his name. “My name is Charley, just Charley,” he whispered.

LONDON, May 5.—(UP)—Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald, who is remaining at the head of the British government despite a risk of blindness, underwent an operation this morning on his right eye. The operation was officially pronounced successful. It was the second eye operation the prime minister has had. He has chosen to remain in office, the United Press learned, although his decision may hasten the apparently inevitable day when he will be totally blind. There is little chance that he can retain his sight if he continues the exacting routine required at No. 10 Downing Street, and he must avoid eye strain and overwork consistently to preserve what strength he has left in his eyes.

| Miami, May 4—U%—A grand jury tonight had under consideration the evidence under which State Attorney N. Vernon Hawthorne asks a murder indictment against Capt. W. N. Lancaster, former British flyer, for the death of Haden Clarke, fiancé of his noted flying partner, Mrs. J. M. Keith-Miller. Clarke, a young writer, was shot to death in the room he shared with Lancaster at the home of Mrs. Keith-Miller here, shortly after Lancaster's return to Miami after being notified Clarke and Mrs. Keith-Miller planned to be married. Both the flyers called the death a suicide, but suicide notes found with the body were called forgeries by a handwriting expert, and the prosecutor said he had obtained Lancaster's admission that he wrote them to avoid suspicion for himself and Mrs. Keith-Miller. Lancaster expressed regret he was not permitted to appear before the grand jury. He said he was confident he c

SHANGHAI, MAY 5. (AP).—Japanese military authorities announced tonight that they had ordered their troops to begin withdrawal from the battalion they now occupy into the international settlement and adjacent areas. It was the first step to carry out an armistice signed this morning to put an end to hostilities between Chinese and Japanese forces which have been going on in the Shanghai sector since January. The armistice, a compromise arrangement which grew out of weeks of negotiations, was signed by Japanese representatives in the hospital here where they are recovering from wounds inflicted by an assassin last week.

1932-03-17.text: Dublin, March 17.—(A. P.)—The wearing of the green had a double significance in Erin today: It was the 1,500th anniversary of St. Patrick’s landing and it brought a new plan for union of the north and south of Ireland. Eamon De Valera, new president of the Free State, announced last night, on the eve of the St. Patrick's day celebrations, a four-point program for his administration, one point of which was an eventual merger of the Free State and Ulster governments, age-old division of Irish affairs. Other points were abolition of the oath of allegiance to King George and of the more than $10,000,000 a year in land annuities paid to the British government, as well as suspension of the military courts set up by the Cosgrave regime to try Irishmen for offenses against the government. The center of the day’s ceremonies in honor of St. Patrick today was at Saul, in County Down, where a giant

WASHINGTON, March 17 (#)—A Democratic attack in the Senate today against revision of the British war debt owed to America brought a denial from Sen. Reed (R., Pa.) on behalf of President Hoover that the subject was even under consideration. Reed specified that the "question had not been discussed," with Ambassador Mellon, who is about to sail for London. Sen. Robinson, of Arkansas, the Democratic leader, had quoted from a newspaper story published here today saying that Mellon was favorably inclined for revision of the British debt. He warned that any revision would be very carefully considered by Congress. Sen. Connally (D., Texas) challenged the administration to state its position. Reed said: "I am authorized to say there is not a word of truth in the newspaper article."

LONDON, Mar. 17. (®)—The Bank of England reduced its discount rate today from four to three and one half per cent. The decision of the bank authorities surprised the market which was not prepared for further reduction after the two recent declines. The monetary situation has grown so easy however and revenue has been coming in so steadily that apparently the bank directors decided to give trade and commerce the benefit of a further half of one percent reduction.

LONDON, March 16, (P)—David Lloyd George re-entered the political arena Wednesday with a challenge to progressive men of all parties to rally round him and save Great Britain from what he declared would be four years of reactionary rule by the “sham” national government. The 69-year old liberal leader, who has been recuperating from an operation, signalled his return to activity by a slashing attack against the MacDonald government in a speech before the junior liberal club. “The national government is a sham—a naked sham or, if not a naked sham, it wears but the meanest of loincloths,” he declared. The crowd jamming the junior liberal club cheered lustily and there were cries of “lead us! lead us!” Mr. Lloyd George indicated he was ready to take the field at the head of the anti-tariff forces. Concerning Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald, Mr. Lloyd George said that “no man can do nothing

Washington, March 17 (4)—Testimonial that the New England Public Service Company spent $200,000 to obtain a favorable vote in a Maine referendum on an act to permit power export was given the federal trade commission today by William T. Chantland, a commission attorney. Chantland, who went to Maine in August 1930 to investigate the expenditure, said he was told by the committee that handled the campaign that the correspondence had been destroyed because the room it occupied was needed. Members of the committee were quoted as saying they believed records of accounts and expenditures of the campaign were sufficient. This testimony was received in the commission's investigation of the Public Service Company after Commissioner McCulloch, who was presiding, ruled it was pertinent. Chantland said members of the committee explained that county chairmen for the campaign had been selected in each

Washington, March 16.—(A.P.)— The United States has joined with Great Britain and other European powers in another protest against slavery conditions in Liberia. Upon the recommendation of the League of Nations commission to make inquiry into the existence of forced labor, of which Samuel Reber, Jr., is the American member, strong representations were made to Liberia on March 7 by the state department against the persecution of Liberian witnesses who testified before the commission. This is the second protest the American state department has made to Liberia.

DUBLIN—(U.P)—The most enthusiastic St. Patrick's day celebration in years was held in Ireland today on the occasion of the 15th century of the Saint's landing. The village of Saul, County Down, where St. Patrick came ashore, was the scene of a time-honored ceremony on the site of a proposed memorial to the Saint. In Dublin, a great throng in the street in front of Trinity College wildly cheered the swearing-in of cabinet member Frank Aiken, minister of defense. Aiken reviewed the Free State army, parading past the national flag in field green uniforms with sprigs of shamrock in their hats. President Eamonn De Valera and members of the cabinet attended high mass at the cathedral celebrated by Archbishop Byrne. Services in Gaelic were held all throughout the country, honoring St. Patrick.

Berlin—The Prussian government accepted a challenge of the forces of Adolf Hitler Thursday, ordering raids on national socialist headquarters throughout the state after disclosures purporting to reveal Nazi plans for a virtual civil war. The ministry of interior issued a statement in which it said its investigation revealed that the Nazis' signal for a march upon the big cities in their neighborhoods was to be the flash “grandmother dead.” The statement said the Hitlerites were ready for a march on Berlin (Continued on Page 2)

1932-11-03.text: By United Press Two crucial battle grounds of the political campaign were in the spotlight today as President Hoover prepared for a fourth invasion of the doubtful middle west and former Governor Alfred E. Smith advanced into New England where Gov. Franklin Roosevelt will center for the next offensive. Political activities, however, stretched to Manila in the Philippine islands, 6,000 miles away, as both parties geared for their final drives of the national campaign. Gov. Gen. Theodore Roosevelt, son of the late President, whose birthday is today, will make an overseas broadcast for the Republican national ticket. Cutting for Roosevelt Across the Mississippi river the battle was intensified as another progressive Republican senator, Cutting of New Mexico, broke from party ranks in a speech at Denver, Col., last night. He called on “all who believe that the common people of America have a

By The Associated Press London, Nov. 2. - After the first contingent of the "hunger-marchers" who swarmed into London last week from all parts of the United Kingdom were started home tonight, the mystery of what happened to their petition, purportedly bearing 1,000,000 names, was solved. The petition, demanding abolition of the means test, which limits dole beneficiaries and which never reached the House of Commons as was intended, was confiscated by police when they learned it had been checked in the Charing Cross Railroad station. Three men presented a check at the station for the bundle tonight and seemed angry when told it had been given to police. The men were informed they would have to make their protest to railroad authorities.

LONDON, Nov. 2,—(UP)—England's “lunger marchers,” disconcerted by the orderly but powerful methods of London's police force to quell their demonstrations, lingered here today, apparently without plans or organization. The show of force by authorities during the attempted march on parliament Tuesday, coupled with the arrest of W. A. L. Hannington, leader of the marchers, apparently disconcerted the marchers. They remained passive during the last 24 hours and no immediate plans for future mass demonstrations were announced. The majority of the unemployed who marched on London from various parts of England, Scotland, and Wales in a protest against the means test applied to the jobless threatened to remain in London, however, until their petition for relief is presented to parliament. The question of their dispersal was the biggest problem confronting the authorities.

LONDON, Nov. 3.—()—Princess Ingrid, the daughter of the Crown Prince of Sweden, left Croydon air-drome for Brussels by plane today after a brief holiday in England as the guest of the Earl of Athlone. The duke bade her farewell at the airport, but, aside from her lady in waiting, the only persons present were fifty cameramen. Rumors of the princess’ engagement to Prince George, fourth son of the king, or the Prince of Wales, were further discounted in official circles today.

- LONDON, Nov. 3 (UP)—Striking again while the invading "hunger army" was disorganized, police today arrested Sid Elias, leader of the demonstrators, in a new drive to destroy an alleged Communist group dominating the unemployed. Elias succeeded to the leadership after the riot which led to the arrest of Steve Hannington, Communist and original leader of the disorders.

BERLIN, Germany, Nov. 3. (4— The train transportation system of Berlin was paralyzed today by a strike against wage cuts affecting 23,000 workers. Police set up a guard after a few conveyances normally used to carry transport employees to work had ventured out, only to be met by a barrage of stones from strike sympathizers. Three men were arrested.

TOULOUSE, France, Nov. 3.— Premier Edouard Herriot’s new disarmament plan calls for abandonment of the rights of neutrality by subscribing nations, it was disclosed today as M. Herriot’s radical socialist party gathered to approve his foreign and other party policies. The convention is expected to give the disarmament project, a part of the foreign policy, the same overwhelming endorsement the premier won in the chamber of deputies last week. It was revealed in connection with the abandonment of neutrality aid, that the disarmament scheme envisaged an anti-war pact with the United States. The report of the party on foreign affairs adds this: “If the United States accepts the Capper resolution to amend the Kellogg pact, a great step toward the problem of the liberty of the seas will have been achieved.” (Senator Arthur Kapper of Kansas has placed a resolution before the United States Sena

Berlin, Nov. 3, (4)—Germany's fascists who wound up the new drive for power were confident that Adolf Hitler will poll next Sunday 40 percent of the vote of the Reich, an increase of three percent over his strength in the last election. On the other hand a spokesman of the government said the “junkers” cabinet of Chancellor von Papen were convinced that Hitler will poll 1,500,000 short of the former election of 14 million votes. Ends Campaign. The Nazi chieftain brought his personal whirlwind campaign to a close last night with an audience of 35,000 persons in the Sports Palast. He attacked Chancellor von Papen as a representative of the “thin upper crust.”

1932-01-29.text: Portland, England, Jan. 29—(P)—The last straw of hope for the rescue alive of any of the sixty-one men and officers who went down with the British submarine M-2 last Tuesday was snatched away today by the publication of an admiralty statement saying it was no longer possible to hope. To Continue Search The statement, which was based upon a report of the rear admiral in charge of submarines, said, however, that the search of the sea floor for the ill-fated submarine would be continued. The object sought by divers yesterday on the theory it might be the M-2 was found to be an old wreck, the admiral said, and the succeeding search will be conducted at another spot where a former sweep brought up two submarine hand flags in a canvas case. Distressed wives and relatives of the men lost their last crumb of comfort with the admiralty’s announcement. Divers Risk Lives Desperate efforts were made

PORTLAND, Eng., Jan. 28.—The submarine M-2 holding three score within her steel hulk, still rolled at the bottom of the English channel tonight and the British admiralty announced the possibility of saving any lives was “almost beyond hope.” Heavy seas and tidal currents late tonight forced divers to give up their attempt to find the submarine until early tomorrow when low tide will be due again. By The Associated Press. PORTLAND, Eng. Jan. 28.—Mysterious tappings under the water were detected today by the Destroyer Thurster on her listening apparatus, and the rescue flotilla looking for the sunken submarine M-2 spurred its operations as night fell. The destroyer had been in the vicinity of the spot where a patch of oil was discovered for several hours when underwater “signals” were first heard. There was a group of naval vessels clustered around the scene as darkness descended and three

Washington, Jan. 29.—Under pressure from the American and British governments, Japan has assured that foreign rights in the international settlement at Shanghai will be respected. Secretary Stimson made the announcement today a short while after meeting with President Hoover and the cabinet in a prolonged session. It seemed evident that a lack of unanimity as to the American course had cropped out at the cabinet meeting, but the various department heads kept what had happened to themselves.

PARIS—Some queer things going on in the world if you just happen to have been there and seen ‘em. Japanese warships are ready to bombard China because China insists on boycotting Japanese goods. England put five hundred more of Gandhi's bunch in jail because they boycott and picket against English goods. Here you have China and India, who constitute five-eighths of the world's population, practically at war because they can't do what they want to, yet sign boards all over England say “Buy British.” It's a great world, even if you are just looking at it for comedy purposes. Yours, WILL ROGERS

LONDON, Jan. 29. (UP)—Hope has been abandoned for rescuing the 60 men aboard the missing submarine M-2, an admiralty statement said today, although a pair of submarine hand flags has been found by minesweepers seeking the lost vessel. Soon after the admiralty statement, the King and Queen sent messages of condolence to the families of the M-2 crew and to all submarine comrades. Experts at the Portland covers examined the submarine flags to see whether they came from the M-2. The statement was based on information received from the commanding officer of submarines definitely admitting "there is no more now of saving life." The submarine was last heard from in the English channel off Portland Tuesday. The admiralty said: "An obstruction discovered six miles north and 30 degrees west of Portland bill was an old wreck. "We shall sweep the vicinity, because an earlier sweep, which parted, bro

By The Associated Press. LONDON, Jan. 28.—The admiralty announced this morning that, in view of a report received from the rear admiral in charge of submarines, it is no longer possible to hope for the rescue of any of the sixty officers and men who were aboard the submarine M-2 when it sank off Portland and that their deaths must now be presumed. The information received from the rear admiral follows: “The obstruction discovered six miles north and thirty degrees west of Portland Bill is an old creek. We shall sweep in the vicinity of an earlier sweep which brought up a pair of submarine hand flags in a canvas case. The general search will continue. We have no hope now of saving life.”

London, Jan. 29—(/P)—Great Britain and the United States will take joint action in dealing with the Chinese crisis it was announced in Downing Street today. The British government has asked the Japanese government to take no action inside the international settlement at Shanghai without prior consultation with the other governments concerned. Great Britain has informed the United States of this action and invited Washington to take a similar step in Tokyo. This was in reply to conversations between Secretary Stimson and representatives of the British government.

WASHINGTON, Jan. 29 (UP)—Secretary of State Stimson announced today the United States and Great Britain had made formal representations to Japan saying they hoped there would be no military occupation of the international settlement at Shanghai unless police were unable to protect Japanese lives and property. France and Italy were advised through their ambassadors here of the Anglo-American action. This was regarded as an informal bid for them also to make representations. Secretary Stimson had not been informed as to what action France and Italy will take. The announcement was made after a cabinet meeting at which President Hoover and his Secretaries discussed a wide range of subjects but gave much attention to the situation in the Far East.

1932-05-31.text: By Associated Press SAUTON, Eng... May 31.—Glenna Collett Vare, five times American golf champion, was defeated in the third round of the British women's golf championship today. Enid Wilson, defending title holder, won 4 and 2.

LONDON, May 31 (P—A mystery involving high London society circles developed today when Michael Scott Stephen was found shot to death in a flat occupied by Mrs. Elvira Dolores Barney, beautiful daughter of a wealthy knight who four years ago married John Sterling Barney, 31, an American banker. The identity of the victim was not established until several hours after the early morning tragedy, which followed a cocktail party. It developed that Mr. Stephen, instead of being a wealthy American, as at first reported, was a member of a widely known English family who has played a prominent part in fashionable west-end life during the last ten years. Scotland Yard got very busy on the mysterious case and Sir Bernard Spilsbury, eminent pathologist, was

| LONDON, May 31. (UP)—That much discussed photograph of an almost nude young girl posing with the Rev. H. F. Davidson, 62-year-old rector on trial before church authorities on immorality charges, was intended for publication in the United States, it turned out today. The mother of the young girl in question so testified before the ecclesiastical court at Church House, Westminster. Photographers had told her, the mother said, that publication in American “might mean a lot for her daughter.” The photograph is an issue in the trial because the prosecution contends it is proof the rector was somewhat indiscreet, and he avers he was trapped into posing—a belief which the girl's mother shares with him. “It was just a disgusting trap well worked out from the beginning,” the mother testified. She had stipulated, she said, that her daughter was not to be photographed in the nude, and to make sur

LONDON, May 30 (#) — Mrs. Amelia Earhart Putnam, first woman solo flier of the Atlantic, was guest today at a hastily arranged tea party in the House of Commons. She was taken to the House by David K. Bruce, son-in-law of Ambassador Andrew W. Mellon. On her appearance the tea party was arranged and nearly all the women members of parliament, including the American-born Lady Astor, were present. Another who was present was J. H. Thomas, secretary for dominions. Mrs. Putnam still was bothered by a cold, which coupled with the many speeches she has been called upon to make since her flight from America, had almost robbed her of her voice.

WANDERLUST, Mess., May 21—(INS)—A thrilling sea-rescue was enacted off Nantucket lightship today when nine men of the Gloucester fishing schooner Irene and Helen were taken from their burning vessel by the coastguard destroyer Tucker, out of New London. The blaze, which started on the schooner as she was returning from the fishing banks, loaded with fish, was sighted by those aboard the lightship. A radio call was sent out, and the Tucker, cruising in the vicinity, responded. A short time after the rescue, the schooner, burned to the water’s edge, sank. The Tucker transferred the men to the Nantucket lightship to await a coastguard cutter from Boston.

Saunton, England, May 31,— Enid Wilson, the defending champion, defeated Mrs. Glenna Collett Vare of Philadelphia, 4 and 2, in a third round match of the British women’s golf championship today. Mrs. Leona Pressier Cheney of Hollywood, Calif., was then the only American remaining in the competition. Mrs. Cheney won her third round match one up, eliminating the British star, Miss Doris Pask.

Berlin, May 31.—Adolf Hitler’s National Socialists today turned their backs on participation in the German government until the verdict of the people has been obtained by general elections following dissolution of the present Reichstag. A spokesman for the Nazis informed the Associated Press that party leaders were certain new elections would give them a clear majority, and in the meantime they would have nothing to do with a stop-gap cabinet. This statement came while President Paul Von Hindenburg, who forced the resignation of Dr. Wilhelm Bruening’s ministry yesterday, was conferring with party leaders in an attempt to provide the nation with a new government. Nazi demonstrations were put on in front of the presidential palace while the conferences were going on. Dr. Ludwig Kaas, in behalf of the Centrists, told the president that in view of the dismissal of Dr. Bruening his party was

VIENNA, May 29 (4)—A mysterious parable writer who signs himself "" and is believed by many to be Gen. Alexandru Averescu, leader of the Rumanian People’s party, caused excitement in Bucharest today with veiled warnings of death for King Carol of Rumania and his friend, Mme. Magda Lupescu. Months ago he hinted strongly at dethronement of the Rumanian king, but recently his writings have taken a more sober turn. A week ago he alluded to the death of the French king, Henry II, in terms leaving no doubt he was warning King Carol. The cafes buzzed today over his latest "history parable" in the people’s party organ, "Indreptarea," which again plays with the death theme in what some readers interpreted as an attack on Madame Lupescu, red-haired companion of Carol's Paris exile before he became king. In this sensational parable, the text of which has appeared in Vienna, "" took as his theme Mad

1932-09-12.text: London, Sept. 12. ()—Mahatma Gandhi has determined to starve himself to death rather than accept the electoral representation system worked out for India by the British cabinet. This was revealed tonight when the India office made public letters that have been exchanged by the Mahatma, Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald and Sir Samuel Hoare, secretary for India. Gandhi intends to take no more food after midday September 20. The Mahatma apologized for any embarrassment he might cause the government, but said he would hold to his decision even if he were released from prison, where he has been kept for months as a result of the conflict between the government and India’s Nationalists. Official sources were unable to say what steps the government was taking to prevent the Mahatma from killing himself by starvation. It is suggested that there was a faint possibility of the Indians agreeing amon

LONDON, Sept. 12—One hundred passengers were reported dead or injured, 600 robbed and many kidnapped by bandits who derailed and attacked a passenger train on the Chinese Eastern railway south of Harbin, Manchuria, yesterday, the Harbin correspondent of the Exchange Telegraph Co. reported today. The bandits, protected by darkness, loosened the rails and swooped down on the train after several coaches left the track. They were reported to have robbed all the 600 passengers and to have carried many away as prisoners. The highest estimate of casualties was 100 dead or wounded. Doctors and nurses were sent to the scene from Harbin at 4 a.m. yesterday. The train was en route from Harbin to Changchun, and was derailed about 30 miles south of Harbin, near Shuenchencu.
